item.title: CLM-JAX v3.2.46: a differentiable, GPU-accelerated land surface model numerically indistinguishable from the Community Land Model 5.0
item.description:
Authors: Shijin Yuan, Zhen Wei, Tianyu Shen, Bin Mu, Bo Qin, Guokun Dai

The original Fortran implementation of the Community Land Model version 5.0 (CLM5.0) primarily targets CPUs and does not support GPU computation or automatic differentiation. We present CLM-JAX, a land surface model implemented in Python, based on the CLM5.0 BGC-Crop configuration in the Community Earth System Model version 2.1.3 (CESM2.1.3). CLM-JAX retains the original subgrid hierarchy, parameterizations and coupling among energy, water, carbon, nitrogen and crop processes, runs on CPUs and GPUs, and supports gradient backpropagation through multi-step time integration

要点：
- 方法：采用机器学习/深度学习模型。

item.title: Predicting acute food crises and discovering actionable drivers with causal machine learning
item.description:
Authors: Mélissande Machefer, Michele Ronco, Michele Meroni, Jordi Cerdà-Bautista, Francesco Collivignarelli, Chungmann Kim, Nicolas Rost, Alessia Matanó

Acute food insecurity is driven by a compound of conflict, adverse climate events, displacement, and economic shocks. We enrich the open-access Harmonized Food Insecurity Dataset with driver variables (monthly, subnational, 80 countries, 2007--2024) and develop missing-data-resilient machine learning pipelines forecasting crisis occurrence at 3, 6, and 9-month lead times using both FEWS NET and, for the first time at scale, IPC/CH classifications. item.title: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
item.description:
Authors: Jinchuan Zhang, Lei Gao, Hongyu Jiang, Chong Mu, Chenang Cai, Ke Yan

Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) continually introduce emerging entities whose interaction histories evolve from zero-shot debuts into sparse, bursty few-shot trajectories. However, current paradigms are fragmented: pattern-transfer methods lack catalog-wide event memory, whereas online memory models suffer from endpoint-role asymmetry that degrades unseen-answer ranking. Furthermore, sparse early interactions exhibit both long-range dispersion and local redundancy under skewed distribution

item.title: ENSO-linked redistribution of post-monsoon tropical cyclone energy between the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal: 1982--2025
item.description:
Authors: Prashant Saini, Rishikesh Yadav, Sarita Azad

Tropical cyclones in the North Indian Ocean (NIO) form in two sub-basins, the Arabian Sea (AS) and the Bay of Bengal (BoB), which are usually studied separately, with their relationship to the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) treated as stationary. We develop a joint inter-basin statistical framework and apply it to 416 disturbances from quality-controlled IBTrACS best tracks for 1982--2025, with harmonised IMD and JTWC intensities, ERA5 and ERSSTv5. item.title: Hierarchical Graph Metanetworks
item.description:
Authors: Ioannis Kalogeropoulos, Giorgos Bouritsas, Yannis Panagakis

The emerging field of weight space learning has demonstrated the potential to enable metanetworks, i.e. models that process neural network (NN) data, to support several steps of the machine learning lifecycle, from model optimisation to evaluation and adaptation. However, this potential has yet to materialise beyond small-scale MLPs or CNNs: most current models, including message-passing based graph metanetworks (GMNs), operate exclusively at the finest level of granularity, processing every neuron and weight of the input model

要点：
- 方法：采用机器学习/深度学习模型。

item.title: When to Trust a PFN: Detecting Harmful Shift in Tabular Foundation Models
item.description:
Authors: Viet Nguyen, Herman Bergström, Stephan Rabanser, Rahul G. Krishnan

Tabular prior-fitted networks (PFNs) work well across tabular classification problems but can fail silently at deployment when distributions shift. We propose CALD (Calibrated Anchor-Loss Disagreement), a lightweight unsupervised monitor that triggers an alarm to warn when a PFN might fail. By finetuning the decoder to maximize disagreement with the test-set prediction while maintaining accuracy on an ID anchor set, CALD identifies harmful OOD batches through the resulting anchor loss, requiring no labels on test batches

要点：
- 数据：包含再分析/卫星/观测等来源。

item.title: Comparative Study of Deep Learning Architectures for Brain Tumour Classification
item.description:
Authors: Prisha Gupta, Pradeep Kumar Gupta

Accurate and early classification of brain tumours from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for treatment planning, yet many published deep learning studies are trained and tested on small, single-source datasets, reporting accuracies that may not hold outside these datasets. item.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction

item.title: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events
item.description:
Authors: Ashkan Golgoon, Giacomo Domeniconi, Samuel Atkins, Sergio Servantez, Zain Khandwala

Autoregressive transformers trained on tokenized tabular event streams are a simple and strong baseline for predicting financial events such as fraud. Yet institutions do not act on probabilities; they act on decisions whose consequences are asymmetric and heteroscedastic: the cost of a missed high-value fraud and that of a wrongly declined small purchase are not the same. The standard bridge is post-hoc Bayes-optimal thresholding of calibrated probabilities under a cost matrix

要点：
- 方法：采用机器学习/深度学习模型。

item.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer

We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops.
